_comment: The diagnostic run: mutants against the hand-written suites only, no differentials.
The gate is stryker.config.json, over the whole suite. This one answers a different
and more useful question: if the frozen oracle vanished tomorrow — which is exactly
what CORE-07 does — would the tests people actually read still pin the behaviour?
The first run said no. 39.88%, with 96 of 127 mutants surviving in sha256.ts, because
the only test touching it asserted `document.digest === sha256Hex(normalize(raw))` —
both sides call the mutated function, so a corrupted round constant changed both and
the assertion still held. test/sha256.test.ts now carries the published FIPS 180-4
vectors instead, and a one-bit change to a round constant fails eight tests.
`break` is null on purpose. This number is a to-do list, not a gate; gating on it
would create pressure to delete the hard mutants rather than write the test.
